intro: Convert megabytes (MB) to gigabytes (GB) instantly for mobile data plans, video file sizes, cloud backups, and SSD partitions. Under the international SI decimal standard used by storage makers and cellular carriers, 1 GB equals 1,000 MB (1 MB = 0.001 GB)—divide MB by 1,000 for a quick megs to gigs conversion. Check decimal and binary-sized file benchmarks from 1 MB to 100,000 MB below.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: SI Decimal (1,000 MB = 1 GB) vs. IEC Binary (1,024 MiB = 1 GiB) & Megabits (Mb)
items: Drive makers, macOS, and mobile carriers use decimal SI (1,000 MB = 1 GB), whereas RAM modules and Windows file properties use binary powers of 1,024 (1,024 MiB = 1 GiB): for example, 6,144 MB = 6.144 GB decimal (or 6 GiB binary), 10,240 MB = 10.24 GB (10 GiB), and 24,576 MB = 24.576 GB (24 GiB).
Do not confuse megabytes (MB, capital B, file size) with megabits (Mb / Mbps, lowercase b, internet speed): 1 byte equals 8 bits, so 100 MB equals 800 megabits.

faqs.question: How many gigabytes are in 1,000 MB vs. 1,024 MB?
faqs.answer: In the SI decimal standard used by SSDs, macOS, and cellular plans, 1,000 MB equals 1 GB (and 1,024 MB equals 1.024 GB). In the IEC binary standard used for RAM and Windows, 1,024 MiB equals 1 GiB.

faqs.question: How do I convert MB to GB?
faqs.answer: Divide the number of megabytes by 1,000 (move the decimal point three places left): GB = MB ÷ 1,000. For example, 21,000 MB ÷ 1,000 = 21 GB.

faqs.question: What are 6,144 MB, 10,240 MB, and 24,576 MB in GB?
faqs.answer: In decimal SI units, 6,144 MB = 6.144 GB, 10,240 MB = 10.24 GB, and 24,576 MB = 24.576 GB. In binary 1,024-based units (GiB), those exact multiples equal 6 GiB, 10 GiB, and 24 GiB.

faqs.question: Why does 100,000 MB equal 100 GB instead of 97.66 GB?
faqs.answer: Because 100,000 ÷ 1,000 = 100 GB in SI decimal storage, whereas dividing by 1,024 yields 97.65625 GiB in binary IEC units—the reason a 100 GB drive reports ~97.66 GiB in Windows.
